planned_reqs.title: kiwi-step lightweight step-local authoring skill
planned_reqs.gist: kiwi-step skill authors requirements only under docs/spec/steps/<name>/, never body-scope SRS. Must claim_step before authoring and run validate_step as part of the authoring workflow.

planned_reqs.title: kiwi-spec-merge per-REQ sequential merge orchestrator skill
planned_reqs.gist: kiwi-spec-merge orchestrates SRS merge as per-REQ, single-REQ operations (dry-run, approval, one mutation call, journal append, resume), never an N-REQ batch finalize. Routes diff_steps classification NEW->promote_step_requirement, UPDATE->in-place body update, CONFLICT->supersede_requirement. On completion migrates loser-side verification evidence and emits a post-merge verification-decrease report.

planned_reqs.title: kiwi-vibe skill for vibe entry
planned_reqs.gist: kiwi-vibe skill elicits implementation intent, accepts an explicit task name or auto-derives one, invokes start_vibe_task with intent-first ordering (intent.md written before Active Task state), and guides the coding agent to insert step task-name trace comments during implementation.

implemented_flow_reqs.title: Versioned agent-instruction governance snippet with idempotent AGENT_INSTRUCTION_VERSION upsert
implemented_flow_reqs.gist: init idempotently upserts a versioned SpecKiwi SRS-workflow governance snippet (MUST rules, Status/Stability, TDD, current-work/next-target workflow) into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md, replacing stale versioned/legacy blocks in place.

implemented_flow_reqs.title: Work-Modes-Rules v1.0.0 bundled rule document and CLAUDE.md reference
implemented_flow_reqs.gist: init writes docs/rule/Work-Modes-Rules-v1.0.0.md (defines sdd/vibe/wait modes, vibe intent-first obligation, task-name question, per-step code-comment convention) write-if-missing, and adds a CLAUDE.md reference line.

implemented_flow_reqs.title: kiwi-vibe-commit skill for trace-to-SRS synthesis
implemented_flow_reqs.gist: kiwi-vibe-commit orchestrates synthesis of the active vibe task into a step-scoped SRS via the vibe-to-SRS synthesis engine, is an idempotent no-op if already synthesized, and hands the synthesized step to kiwi-spec-merge (FR-FLOW-015) for per-REQ promotion.

implemented_flow_reqs.title: Code comment trace-tag convention for sdd and vibe modes
implemented_flow_reqs.gist: Defines the @req <REQ-ID> comment convention for sdd-mode changes and the active-step-task-name tag for vibe-mode changes; purely informational, gates nothing.

implemented_flow_reqs.title: Init-injected agent instruction block declares a tool-first SRS policy
implemented_flow_reqs.gist: init idempotently injects a versioned managed block into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (and the bundled SRS-MD-Rules doc) declaring MCP-first / CLI-fallback tool policy and forbidding an alternate requirements source outside docs/spec/.

additional_observations: All 5 implemented FLOW-scope requirements (016,017,019,020,021) are either documentation/governance-snippet requirements (016,017,020,021 = layer 'other') or an orchestration skill (019 = layer 'skill'). None of the implemented FLOW-scope requirements specify runtime step/vibe mutation behavior themselves; the actual runtime backing for claim_step/validate_step/diff_steps/promote_step_requirement/supersede_requirement/start_vibe_task lives entirely outside FLOW scope, split across MCP scope (tool registration) and NODE/PARSE scope (core implementation).

FR-FLOW-019 (implemented, kiwi-vibe-commit) already hands its output to FR-FLOW-015 (planned, kiwi-spec-merge) per its own requirement text ('after synthesis it SHALL hand the resulting step off to the kiwi-spec-merge skill (FR-FLOW-015)'). This means an implemented, presumably-in-use skill requirement already presumes the existence of a still-planned skill requirement.

The FR-NODE ID citations embedded in FR-MCP-042/043/044 and FR-FLOW-019 requirement prose are a consistent +15 off from the correct IDs (e.g. FR-NODE-027 -> FR-NODE-042, FR-NODE-041 -> FR-NODE-056), consistent with a renumbering event in docs/spec/50.nodejs-implementation.srs.md that was not propagated to cross-references in prose text. The underlying capabilities themselves are present and implemented under the correct (uncited) IDs.
